what_worked: Exceptional framing of limitations, power-law thesis sustained throughout, and genuinely useful category-vs-revenue bubble chart.
fix_next: Multiple category medians (Education, Marketing, Analytics) are substantially wrong; verify every computed statistic against raw data before presenting.
verdict: Strong narrative and design undermined by numerous factual errors in core statistics.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: anonymous count 72 vs actual 129. Slide 3: top-10 share 50.6% vs 49.6%. Slide 7: Education median $2,142 vs $2,435; Marketing median $1,586 vs $2,369.50; Analytics median $1,294 vs $419. Slide 9: Stripe revenue share 89.7% vs 86.7%.

evidence.insight: Slide 9 B2B pricing-not-scale decomposition is genuinely original; slide 11 pricing anomaly (similar multiples despite 5.7× MRR gap) is a real finding. Slide 6 bubble chart reframes AI crowding effectively.
evidence.narrative: Clear five-act structure: universe → concentration → categories → monetisation → exits. Each slide builds on the power-law thesis. Conclusion slide synthesizes coherently.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 'Read this before you trust any chart' box is exemplary: declares no time dimension, self-selection bias, and disclosure gaps upfront. Consistent footer with caveats on every slide.
evidence.accuracy: Six material errors: anonymous count off by 57 (slide 2), top-10 share inflated ~1pp (slide 3), three category medians substantially wrong (slide 7 — Analytics off by 3×), Stripe share inflated 3pp (slide 9).
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with clear hierarchy. Lorenz curve (slide 3), log-log bubble chart (slide 6), and growth histogram (slide 10) are well-chosen. Annotations are purposeful. Side panels with key stats aid scanning.
